messages:

Subject: Initial SSQ + dataflow for subprocessor onboarding

Marcus / Monica –

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our completed Security & Privacy questionnaire (MedLink_SSQ_v2.pdf) and a Visio of the dataflow (medlink_dataflow.vsdx). We flagged a few areas where we need clarity from vendors: tokenization/redaction approach for PII in transit, KMS custody for token mapping, and the list of subprocessors that will see raw PII during onboarding.

High-level asks:
- Can you confirm which Redwood subprocessors will have access to raw PII (if any) during ingestion and initial validation?
- What controls will be used to ensure tokens cannot be reverse-mapped outside of our environment?
- Do you have a preferred artifact for DPA Annex updates (PDF + signed DocuSign OK)?

Attachments:
- MedLink_SSQ_v2.pdf (PDF)
- medlink_dataflow.vsdx (Visio)

We've got a compliance review scheduled next Tuesday; would appreciate a short response with named owners and a suggested plan by EOD Monday PST.

Best,
Aisha Mirza
Director, Privacy & Controls
MedLink Health

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Mirza <aisha@medlink.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ + dataflow for subprocessor onboarding

Aisha —

Thanks for the packet and the diagram. We're happy to run the onboarding with the controls you need. Quick summary of our approach and proposed owners:

1) Subprocessors and raw PII access
- Short answer: the standard hosted pipeline routes ingestion through our ingestion service (redwood-ingest) and a small set of telemetry/sanitization workers (subprocessors). During onboarding we may temporarily route verification artifacts to a human review queue; those are cryptographically protected and access is limited to a named team.
- Owners: marcus_lin (procurement/controls lead), monica_patel (security ops), rachel_kim (privacy liaison).

2) Tokenization/redaction model
- Proposal: we will apply deterministic tokenization for identifiers (SSNs, MRNs) at the ingestion edge and store token->value mapping in a customer-scoped KMS-wrapped vault. Token mapping keys are protected with per-customer key policy in KMS; only the customer and an emergency unseal role in Redwood (two-person approval) can request decryption.
- For free-text PII we will run a redaction pass using our PII-detection model and replace spans with hashed tokens before persistence. The redaction spec is attached (redaction_spec.md).

3) Preventing reverse-mapping
- We use salted hashing + envelope encryption; salts are per-customer and managed in the KMS. Additionally, we can set shortened retention for token mapping (e.g., 30 days) if MedLink prefers ephemeral mappings during onboarding.

4) DPA Annex & signing
- We can provide a PDF annex and a DocuSign-ready package. Draft will be prepared by our contracts team.

Next steps (proposed):
- Monday EOD PST: we deliver a concise onboarding playbook (controls, subprocessors list, runbook for manual review) — owner: marcus_lin.
- Tue: 30-min sync with your compliance team to walk the diagram and KMS approach — owner: monica_patel.

CCing Rachel & Monica to capture any gaps. If you want us to mark fields in your SSQ directly, we can return an annotated copy.

Attachments: redaction_spec.md (Markdown)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: MedLink onboarding playbook outline

Team —

Following Marcus' reply, here's an internal outline I drafted for the onboarding playbook we should send Monday:

1) Executive summary (1 page) — what MedLink can expect during the onboarding window (48–72 hours for data ingest verification).
2) Subprocessor roster (table) — roles, brief justification, access boundary, retention.
3) Dataflow diagram (annotated) — call out where tokenization + redaction occur; include drive link.
4) KMS custody and keypolicy — steps for customer key import, emergency unseal procedure, rotation cadence.
5) Validation runbook — how to request temporary replays, manual review escalation path, logs and audit trail locations.
6) DPA annex process — draft timeline, signature steps, and a sample clause for token mapping custody and retention.

Open questions for Monday sync:
- Do we offer the ephemeral token mapping (30-day retention) by default for onboarding? I think yes for MedLink, but want Neha's take on risk and controls.
- For the human-review queue, can we guarantee that reviewers never receive the full MRN unless they perform a redaction verification step that is logged and time-limited?

Neha — could you add recommended wording for the DPA clause (custody & emergency unseal) and a suggested retention default?

-rk

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 00:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: MedLink onboarding playbook outline

Rachel / team —

Draft clause language below and I also prepared a redlined DPA annex (DPA_Annex_MedLink_20261130.pdf) that includes the wording. I'll attach the DocuSign bundle when legal gives a final thumbs-up.

Proposed clause (for DPA annex) — short form for playbook: 
"Redwood will perform tokenization and deterministic mapping for specified identifiers. Token mapping material is stored in a customer-isolated vault encrypted with keys under the customer's control (customer KMS). Redwood personnel may access mapping values only under documented emergency unseal procedures that require two named approvers and audit logging. Temporary, limited-scope access (for onboarding verification) may be granted for up to 30 days unless otherwise agreed; such access is subject to least-privilege, just-in-time elevation, and explicit customer approval recorded in the audit trail."

Suggested retention default: 30 days for onboarding mappings, 0–7 days for ephemeral verification artifacts if MedLink requires more strict limits.

Actionable items I will deliver by EOD Monday PST:
- Redlined DPA annex (attached)
- Short onboarding playbook PDF with the annotated dataflow (we'll export the Visio to PNG overlays)
- Updated subprocessors list with role-level access notes

Once we have MedLink's confirmation on retention preference I will finalize the annex.

-Neha
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
